Package src

Class Gateway

java.lang.Object
java.rmi.server.RemoteObject
java.rmi.server.RemoteServer
java.rmi.server.UnicastRemoteObject
src.Gateway
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Remote, GatewayInterface
public class Gateway extends UnicastRemoteObject implements GatewayInterface
The Gateway class serves as a central coordinator in a distributed indexing system. It maintains a registry of IndexStorageBarrel instances, manages URL distribution for indexing, and keeps track of system status and search frequencies.

    • getSystemStatus

      public String getSystemStatus() throws RemoteException
      Retrieves the current status of the system, including information about top searches across all barrels and the average response times of active barrels. The method compiles and returns a detailed status report, which includes: - The top 10 search terms used across all barrels, sorted by their frequency. - The active status of each barrel and its average response time.
      Specified by:
      getSystemStatus in interface GatewayInterface
      Returns:
      A string representation of the system status.
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if a networking error occurs.

    • main

      public static void main(String[] args)
      The main method to start the Gateway server. This method initializes the Gateway with the required configurations and starts the RMI registry.
      Parameters:
      args - Command line arguments. The first argument should be the RMI Registry port number. The second argument should be the IP address of the Gateway. The remaining arguments should be the IP addresses of the Index Storage Barrel (ISB) machines. Usage: java Gateway RMI_Registry_Port Gateway_IP_Address> ISB_Machine_IP1 [...ISB_Machine_IPn] Example: java Gateway 1099 192.168.1.2 192.168.1.3 192.168.1.4 This method will exit if the necessary arguments are not provided. It sets the 'java.rmi.server.hostname' property to ensure RMI uses the correct network interface. The 'sun.rmi.transport.tcp.responseTimeout' is also set for handling RMI response timeouts. If an exception occurs during the initialization or binding process, it will be printed to the standard error.
